universalAnswers.whatHappened: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5 on September 8, adding Sketch, templates, image comments and prompt sharing.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: It is the image-making and image-editing part of ChatGPT—not a new general chat model.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: OpenAI's release, current release notes and system card, plus a bounded Axios hands-on report.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The speed and broad quality claims remain vendor claims; Axios tested only a small set of tasks.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Readers can guide layout with a sketch and point to a targeted change instead of encoding the whole visual job in prose.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: ChatGPT users making or editing images, including people planning presentations, social posts, rooms and other visual work.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The new tools are rolling out now; templates are not yet in Work mode and account timing can vary.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Independent broad evaluation is not yet available, and exact consistency will vary by task.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Try one layout-sensitive task with a rough sketch and one targeted edit, then check copy, measurements and important facts outside the image.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Does this input method give me more control over the result I actually need?

model-tool-release.productRange: ChatGPT Images 2.5 is the image generation and editing part of ChatGPT; Flare and Sunburst are separate developer API routes.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: Sketch, templates, comments placed on images and optional prompt sharing are newly announced product controls.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Early layout exploration, visual variations and focused edits where showing the arrangement is easier than describing it.
model-tool-release.notFor: It is not a fully layered design file, proof of exact text or measurements, or a replacement for final factual and brand checks.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: A text-only image prompt remains available; the new routes add visual context and a marked edit target.
model-tool-release.availability: Rolling out on desktop, mobile and web across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex; exact timing may vary.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: OpenAI says all ChatGPT tiers; existing image-generation limits remain and templates are not yet in Work mode.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: No new consumer price is announced; all tiers does not mean unlimited generations.
model-tool-release.limitations: Rollout timing, plan limits, lack of editable layers and limited independent testing remain important boundaries.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: The article uses a room and social-post layout to explain the input method, not to claim professional production readiness.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: Feature and speed claims are attributed to OpenAI; Axios supplies only bounded first-hand corroboration.

translation.newsVersionExact: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.5 on September 8.
translation.actualMeaningExact: The practical change is not simply that the pictures may look better. It is that you can communicate visually instead of trying to describe every detail in one long prompt.
translation.mechanismExact: A sketch gives the system a rough map: put the sofa here, leave space for a headline there, or make the product the largest object. A comment gives it a smaller editing target: change this sleeve, remove that lamp, keep the rest.
translation.familiarExampleExact: Someone planning a room could draw the furniture placement instead of writing a paragraph about left, right and centre.

jargon.plainMeaning: It is the image-making and image-editing part of ChatGPT—not a new general chat model.
Because this is a rollout, a feature may not appear in every account at the same moment.

learningConnections.learningPayoff: Understand why a sketch, marked region or file can guide the system differently from prose alone.
